title: Hydraulic water locks used to float blocks up into the pyramid, with remnants seen in SAR tags
summary: Jeffrey tells of Hydraulic water locks used to float blocks up into the pyramid, with remnants seen in SAR tags, about 2021 at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: So, there have been researchers that have proposed that there was a system of locks, hydraulic locks, that were used to move blocks up into the pyramids.
these could be remnants or vestiges of a water lock system that were used to move blocks up into the pyramid.
tellings.difference: Calls the features possible remnants of the lock system and does not mention the SAR data.
tellings.link_reason: The same water lock theory for moving blocks into the pyramid that telling 1 tells, from the same teller.

as_told.title: Water lock system used to move blocks

plain: A researcher named Jeffrey, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show and pointing back to a video he made in 2021, says some researchers have proposed that the Great Pyramid in Giza, Egypt, was built using a system of water locks, like those on a canal, to float the huge stone blocks up into place. He suggests certain features, which he ties to SAR scans (a kind of radar imaging that can look beneath the ground), could be leftovers of that lock system, though in another telling he simply calls them possible remnants without mentioning the radar. If true, it would change how people think the pyramid was built.
